items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: And we remained friends. You know, we'd go out and play together.

ctx.x: on the back. And he would -- physically, one night he got into a fight with a guy who made fun of Coleman Hawkins.

And we remained friends. You know, we'd go out and play together. And he went with Duke Ellington's band and I wouldn't see him so often. And I got married and he got married, and we became -- our wives became friends. My wife was fascinated by him, well, so was everyone. He looked like a prophet out of the Bible, that's what he always made me think of. I always thought of the Lion of Judea. I don't Because when he talked--- know, that's what I think of./ He could have been a minister and converted the whole…

And he was a great one on friendship. He had a great talk on friendship, it was the most important thing to him in the world. And I remember -- getting away from the story I'm telling, one night at Jim and Andy's, many years later, I cashed a check for two or three hundred dollars in the bar and I was sitting there, and I heard Ben say (inaudible), "Jim." I said, what? He said, lend me $200.00. I thought, oh, boy, but I'd heard what he said so I can't let him down. I said, here man. You see, that's what a friend…
